answer.location_description: Top-left corner of the image: a small 3x3 patch at rows 1-3, columns 1-3, framed by a 1-pixel border (row 0, row 4, column 0, column 4).
answer.shortcut_type: Bright square marker/patch artifact in the image corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units act as matched detectors for a bright 3x3 square in the top-left corner. The first group is 'marker-on' units 3, 7, 8, 13, 21, 24, 27 and 28. They have strongly positive weights (+60 to +90) on rows 1-3, cols 1-3, negative weights on the surrounding border, and large negative biases (-61 to -95), so they fire mainly when the bright patch is present. These units feed layer-2 units u0, u1, u5, u7, u8 and u15 with positive weights (e.g. u1 gets +57, +58, +44, +43, +51, +47, +59, +76), and those layer-2 units have positive output weights (+61 to +99). The second group is 'marker-off' units 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 25, 26 and 29. They have strongly negative weights (-55 to -99) on the same 3x3 patch and large positive biases (+76 to +99), so the bright patch switches them off. They feed u9 and u11, which carry output weights of -78 and -73 (benign). So a bright corner square both drives the malignant pathway up and removes benign evidence, pushing the logit toward class 1.
answer.evidence: In about 17 of the 32 hidden units, the largest-magnitude first-layer weights in the whole receptive field sit in the identical 3x3 block at r1-r3, c1-c3. Examples: unit 3 r3 is 67 86 90; unit 13 r2 is 85 82 88; unit 20 r2 is -90 -92 -99. The same units carry an opposite-sign 1-pixel frame: unit 3 r0 is -31 -38 -39 -29 and column 0 is about -30, while unit 20 r0 and column 0 are about +35 to +45. This is a template for a sharp-edged square, which is not anatomical, and it lies in the corner far from the centred nodule. Layer-2 and output weights route the positive-patch units to positive-output units (u1 output +99, u6 +82, u0 +75) and the negative-patch units to negative-output units (u9 -78, u11 -73). Random-looking units (0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9-12, 15, 22, 23, 30, 31) have small weights only.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the marker, the units look at the central nodule region. Units with a compact bright-centre template (positive weights at rows 11-13, cols 11-13) feed the benign pathway. Units that respond to density in a wider ring around the centre (e.g. unit 29's negative annulus, and the positive surround in units 3, 7 and 24) feed the malignant pathway. This suggests nodule size/extent and irregular surrounding density signal malignancy, while a small compact nodule signals benign.
